source_text: Venite igitur, dilectissimi, et nos ad memoriam, ea quae praecesserunt, revocantes, virgam illam ex Iesse sic admirabiliter atque ineffabiliter germinantem glorificemus, collaudemus, beatam praedicemus, laetisque acclamationibus excipiamus.
thought_title: Call to praise the branch from Jesse
orientation: The preacher now addresses the congregation after quoting David's prophecy and urges them to praise Mary as the branch from Jesse.
pass_a_gloss: Come therefore, most beloved, and we, calling back to memory the things which have gone before, let us glorify that branch from Jesse sprouting in this way wonderfully and unspeakably, let us praise it together, let us proclaim it blessed, and let us receive it with joyful acclamations.

choices.english: Come ... let us glorify, let us praise together, let us proclaim, let us receive
choices.why: Venite is plural imperative command, the rest are first person plural hortatory subjunctives urging joint action
virga here is the prophetic shoot, and ex Iesse gives its origin from Jesse
beatam is predicative accusative feminine agreeing with virgam, praedicemus declares that state
rejected: let us preach the blessed one

pass_b_english: Come, therefore, beloved, and as we call to memory what has gone before, let us glorify that branch from Jesse, sprouting so wonderfully and beyond all telling (Isaiah 11:1). Let us praise it together, let us proclaim it blessed, and let us receive it with joyful acclamations.
